Metrics.KafkaDiagnosticSamplingNote: Outbox and Kafka stage timer count/sum snapshots include warmup; stage times are seconds. All native consumer client series are preserved; commit latency is a rolling Kafka statistic in milliseconds, not terminal P95. Committed group lag is cached and must be read with last-success/failure values; missing and non-finite values remain unknown.
Metrics.ResourceSamplingNote: docker stats samples only disposable Campaign/Worker MySQL, Kafka and Redis containers. Campaign/Worker JVM CPU is sampled from Windows process cumulative CPU time and reported as percent of one logical core. Queue active row count/oldest age, Campaign Hikari gauges, bounded draw-queue processing outcome counters/timer sums, draw transaction and low-cardinality repository segment timer counts/sums, and sampled MySQL InnoDB lock-wait relationships are sampled every 5s. Lock waits are point-in-time samples and transient waits may be missed. Memory percentage uses Docker-reported limits. Same-host generator and control-query overhead are present. An exceeded stop threshold fails this bounded stage and blocks using it to justify a higher stage.

Note: Single Windows host with disposable containers, one Campaign queue consumer and one Worker; synthetic tokens are held only in a temporary local file and removed during cleanup. Not production capacity or HA evidence.
